---
title: "06 — Calibrate predictions using 2024"
output: html_notebook
---

**Measures:** whether probabilities predicted by the already-fitted models match observed frequent mental distress in a later year. Calibrators use 2024 outcomes only. They do not refit the base classifier and never see 2025 outcomes.


## Setup

Loads the unchanged input settings, shared model functions, and the persistent run
increment. The output suffix identifies this run.

```{r setup}
# Set the project root, then load R code from the shared R Notebooks.

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Project-root discovery
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Search upward for the project marker so notebook paths do not depend on a particular
# subfolder.
find_project_root <- function(start = getwd()) {
    current <- normalizePath(start, mustWork = TRUE)
    # Walk toward the filesystem root until the project marker is found.
    repeat {
        if (file.exists(file.path(current, "FMD_Project.Rproj"))) {
            return(current)
        }
        # Move up one directory; an unchanged parent marks the filesystem root.
        parent <- dirname(current)
        if (identical(parent, current)) {
            stop("Open FMD_Project.Rproj in RStudio first")
        }
        current <- parent
    }
}


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Notebook execution root
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Resolve the project before loading modules; configure subsequent knitr chunks to use
# that root.
project_root <- find_project_root()
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = project_root)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Shared-module loader
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Extract R chunks in source order and evaluate them in the caller environment.
# This lightweight loader does not process chunk options such as eval = FALSE.
load_module <- function(name) {
    path <- file.path(project_root, "R", paste0(name, ".Rmd"))
    text <- readLines(path, warn = FALSE)
    starts <- which(startsWith(text, "```{r"))
    ends <- which(trimws(text) == "```")
    blocks <- lapply(starts, function(start) {
        # Use the next standalone closing fence for this R chunk.
        finish <- ends[ends > start][1]
        if (is.na(finish) || finish <= start + 1L) {
            stop("Missing code or closing fence in ", path)
        }
        paste(text[(start + 1L):(finish - 1L)], collapse = "\n")
    })
    eval(parse(text = paste(blocks, collapse = "\n\n")), envir = parent.frame())
    invisible(TRUE)
}


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Shared settings and utilities
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Load configuration before helpers, retaining the existing presentation palette module.
load_module("config")
load_module("run_manager")
load_module("helpers")
load_module("plot_palette")

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Existing-run attachment
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Attach to an allocated run rather than incrementing the counter in this stage.
run_context <- attach_run()
cat("[RUN] Current increment:", run_context$id, "\n")
```


## Fit frozen probability adjustments

Platt-style logistic calibration fits an intercept and slope to the model logit. Audits
both raw and adjusted probabilities on the calibration year.

```{r fit-frozen-probability-adjustments}
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Calibration using 2024 outcomes
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Keep base classifiers fixed while fitting an intercept and slope to their log-odds.
# Audit adjusted predictions on the same calibration year, not an independent evaluation
# sample.

calibration <- load_run_rds("checkpoints", "02_calibration_2024")
calibrators <- list()
rows <- list()


# Iterate through the configured analysis items in the original execution order.
for (family in c("logistic", "lasso", "forest")) {
    fitted <- load_run_rds("models", paste0("05_", family))
    raw_probability <- predict_classifier(fitted, calibration)
    log_odds <- stats::qlogis(pmin(1 - 1e-6, pmax(1e-6, raw_probability)))
    calibration_data <- data.frame(
        outcome = calibration$FMD,
        score = log_odds,
        model_weight = normalize_weights(calibration$RAW_WEIGHT)
    )
    calibrator <- suppressWarnings(stats::glm(
        outcome ~ score,
        data = calibration_data,
        family = stats::binomial(),
        weights = model_weight,
        control = stats::glm.control(maxit = 60)
    ))
    if (!isTRUE(calibrator$converged) || any(!is.finite(stats::coef(calibrator)))) {
        stop("2024 calibrator failed for ", family)
    }

    coefficient <- as.numeric(stats::coef(calibrator))
    calibrators[[family]] <- list(
        intercept = coefficient[1],
        slope = coefficient[2],
        fitted_year = calibration_year
    )
    adjusted <- calibrate_probabilities(raw_probability, coefficient[1], coefficient[2])
    rows[[family]] <- data.table::rbindlist(list(
        data.frame(
            family = family, version = "raw",
            weighted_metrics(calibration$FMD, raw_probability, calibration$RAW_WEIGHT)
        ),
        data.frame(
            family = family, version = "calibrated",
            weighted_metrics(calibration$FMD, adjusted, calibration$RAW_WEIGHT)
        )
    ))
}


# Persist this run-specific object for downstream stages without intentionally
# overwriting an existing artifact.
save_once_rds(calibrators, "models", "06_frozen_calibration")
calibration_audit <- data.table::rbindlist(rows)

# Save this result under the attached run ID so it remains linked to the current
# analysis.
save_table(calibration_audit, "06_2024_calibration_audit")
print(calibration_audit)
```


## Visualize calibration change

Compares raw versus recalibrated Brier scores on 2024. This is fit-year performance, not
an independent test of the calibration step.

```{r visualize-calibration-change}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Visualize the effect of 2024 recalibration
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# Compare each model's Brier score before and after
# recalibration on the 2024 calibration sample.
#
# Positive values indicate an improvement.
# These are fitting-year results, not independent tests.

calibration_effect <- data.table::dcast(
    calibration_audit,
    family ~ version,
    value.var = "brier"
)

calibration_effect[
    ,
    `:=`(
        brier_reduction = raw - calibrated,
        reduction_pct = 100 * (raw - calibrated) / raw
    )
]

calibration_effect[
    ,
    family := factor(
        family,
        levels = c("forest", "lasso", "logistic")
    )
]

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Construct the visualization
# ------------------------------------------------------------

plot <- ggplot2::ggplot(
    calibration_effect,
    ggplot2::aes(
        x = reduction_pct,
        y = family
    )
) +
    ggplot2::geom_segment(
        ggplot2::aes(
            x = 0,
            xend = reduction_pct,
            yend = family
        ),
        color = atg_palette[["evergreen"]],
        linewidth = 1.3
    ) +
    ggplot2::geom_point(
        color = atg_palette[["evergreen"]],
        size = 3.5
    ) +
    ggplot2::geom_text(
        ggplot2::aes(
            label = sprintf("%.2f%%", reduction_pct)
        ),
        hjust = -0.2,
        size = 4
    ) +
    ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(
        labels = function(x) {
            sprintf("%.1f%%", x)
        },
        expand = ggplot2::expansion(
            mult = c(0, 0.23)
        )
    ) +
    atg_theme() +
    ggplot2::labs(
        title = "How much did 2024 recalibration improve predictions?",
        subtitle = "Relative reduction in survey-weighted Brier score",
        x = "Brier score reduction (higher is better)",
        y = "Model family",
        caption = paste(
            "Recalibration and evaluation both use 2024 outcomes.",
            "These gains are descriptive fitting-year results;",
            "2025 is reserved for independent evaluation."
        )
    )

show_and_save(
    plot,
    "06_calibration_brier_improvement",
    9,
    5
)
```
